post.caption:
The grid stores almost nothing, so generation is matched to demand live, every second. Frequency is the dial that shows whether the match is holding: too much demand drags generators slower, too little lets them run fast. Which is why operators forecast things like the end of a popular broadcast, when everyone switches a kettle on at once. And when the balance breaks, equipment disconnects to protect itself, which unbalances everything else. That cascade is a blackout.
